scope: ByteNN FP32 operators in pinned Natural model; static instruction audit plus synthetic ARM64 kernel emulation. Not full-engine or device equivalence.

tensor_layout.proof: Tensor initializer0x5805c stores four extents and multiplies element_count. Concat copies per-pixel channel spans; synthetic non-square and batch-two input verifies extent order.

concat.operation: concatenate channels in graph input order; ONNX NCHW axis1
concat.graph_scope: Observed Natural Concat nodes are all arity2
proof: 0x795dc..0x79614 sums tensor+0x30, preserves first three extents, initializes output
0x7a2cc..0x7a2ec memcpy C0 floats then C1 floats for same pixel
0x7a304..0x7a308 increments source pointers by each channel-byte count

eltwise.operation: float32 elementwise addition, then max(sum,0) iff final graph flag is nonzero
eltwise.broadcast: No broadcast claimed; pinned graph uses equal shapes
proof: 0x6ea14..0x6ea24 final numeric token normalized to boolean at layer+0x108
0xe0d38..0xe0d54 scalar add then same gated zero-clamp

upsampling.operation: 2x bilinear spatial resize with half_pixel coordinates and clamp edges
upsampling.coordinate: src = dst * 0.5 - 0.25; floor index; fraction zero at clamped edges
proof: 0x70480..0x704b8 compute first axis indices/weights, clamp negatives and last edge
upsampling.limit: Static coordinate proof; kernel emulation here does not test full resize implementation.

tanh.native_vector_numerics: Approximate exponential polynomial followed by unrefined FRECPE reciprocal estimate. Not bitwise same as high-precision ONNX Tanh.
tanh.native_scalar_tail: expf call then scalar divide and subtract

kernel_replay.scope: original ARM64 kernel emulation on synthetic input; no complete original-engine execution

tanh.native_implementation: polynomial exp + ARM64 FRECPE reciprocal estimate, scalar expf tail

limitations: The emulated external memcpy is a byte copy; scalar expf uses Python libm then float32 rounding, not Android libm. NEON polynomial/FRECPE kernel instructions themselves are emulated.

Synthetic kernel tests validate local data layout and operator interpretation; do not establish native full-graph engine parity, selected optimization paths, active device identity, face preprocessing, style composition, HDR support or complete application integration.
ONNX high precision Tanh intentionally differs from original approximate Tanh; report a mathematical reconstruction/high precision replacement, never exact original inference parity.
